Operational foundation

VRPTW formulation aligns cost and workload measures

One route-distance vector connects feasibility, workload, and equity reporting.

C ⋅ R = s u m j ⋅ c ⋅ R j
One measurable foundation
Route distance is both the workload quantity and the basis for the equity metrics.
How the alignment works
Feasibility: each customer is served once, with depot, capacity, and time-window constraints.
Workload: each route’s workload is its travel distance.
Reporting: CV, Gini, and Jain use the same nonempty route-distance vector.
dᵣ
Distance traveled by route r; the shared workload unit.
D
The vector of nonempty route distances used for comparison.
μ
Average route distance; the workload reference point.
σ
Spread of route distances around the average.
CV
Primary workload-equity metric: variation normalized by the average route distance.
